back: Two real numbers or expressions related by <, >, ≤, ≥. Numerical: 3<5. Literal: x<5. Double: 3<5<7.
Strict: <, > . Slack: ≤, ≥ . Strict excludes endpoint; slack includes it.

front: Linear in one vs two variables
back: ax+b<0 (a≠0) → one variable. ax+by<c (a≠0,b≠0) → two variables. ax²… is quadratic, not linear.
Value making inequality true is a solution; set of all such values is solution set. For 30x<200, trial gives {0,1,2,3,4,5,6} for whole-number packets.
Same number may be added/subtracted to both sides without changing sign.
By positive → sign stays. By negative → sign reverses (<→>, ≤→≥). Example: 3>2 but −3<−2.
(a,b) open, [a,b] closed, [a,b) , (a,b]. (−∞,2) means x<2. [8,∞) means x≥8.
x<a: open circle at a, line left. x≥a: dark circle at a, line right. Dark = included.
Solve each separately, then intersect. Example: x<6 and x≥2 → 2≤x<6 = [2,6). Graph is overlapping bold segment.
'at least 60' → ≥60, 'less than 40' → <40, 'at most 60' → ≤60. Translate English word to sign first.
Never forget to flip when dividing by negative. For −5x ≤ −40 → x≥8 (not x≤8).
